summary: On the assigned MI350X, the prepared base still weak-referenced SGLang breakable-graph inputs. Two 512 KiB tensor shapes reproduced exact shared-pool pointer reuse, bridge corruption, and reverse clobbering; strong-reference controls stayed intact. The actual SGLang bridge regression failed before and passed after retaining captured args and kwargs strongly.

tests.what_was_measured: ROCm graph-pool pointer reuse, bridge values after a later bucket capture, reverse clobbering after earlier graph replay, and strong-reference controls for shapes (64, 2048) and (128, 1024). Raw output: /job/artifacts/j-f5b1caf0c0ad/model_free_reproducer.log

Failing-before regression against the actual checked-out SGLang breakable graph bridge: both shapes reused the captured break-input pointer. Raw output: /job/artifacts/j-f5b1caf0c0ad/before_actual_bridge.log
Passing-after actual bridge regression for both shapes plus all nearby basic capture/replay tests: 10 passed and 2 subtests passed. Raw output: /job/artifacts/j-f5b1caf0c0ad/after_bridge_suite.log

gpu_execution.evidence: Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 (HIP 7.2.26015) executed graph capture and replay on one visible AMD Instinct MI350X. Weak references reused identical addresses and produced [-999, -999, -999, -999] bridge reads followed by [7, 7, 7, 7] reverse clobbering for both shapes.

remaining_limitations: No large-model, greedy-output, throughput, or memory-overhead validation was performed; the model-free result does not establish those issue claims.
No compiler or ISA claim was made, and no native rebuild was required because the fix is confined to Python reference lifetime.
The ROCm runtime warned that host NUMA balancing is enabled; node-wide configuration was intentionally left unchanged and did not prevent deterministic reproduction or validation.
